claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 consolidated by SPS at approximately 1700 °C can become fully or nearly fully dense.
SPS at approximately 1700 °C can produce a fine-grained ZrB2 microstructure.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 produced above 2300 °C typically has coarse grains.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 produced above 2300 °C typically retains residual porosity.
Coarse grains and residual porosity limit the oxidation resistance of conventionally processed ZrB2.
Coarse grains and residual porosity make conventionally processed ZrB2 susceptible to degradation in liquid plating environments.
Traditional processing below 1700 °C yields ZrB2 with insufficient densification.
Traditional processing below 1700 °C yields ZrB2 with compromised structural integrity.
Rapid heating and applied pressure during SPS promote fast densification of ZrB2.
Rapid SPS densification minimizes grain growth and porosity in ZrB2.
SPS preserves the intrinsic strong covalent bonding and high-melting character of ZrB2.
A fine-grained, uniformly dense ZrB2 microstructure provides enhanced grain-boundary strength.
A fine-grained ZrB2 microstructure promotes rapid formation of a stable, protective oxide scale during high-temperature exposure.
Reduced porosity decreases pathways for infiltration by liquid plating metal.
SPS-processed ZrB2 should have mechanical strength comparable to or greater than conventionally sintered ZrB2 at room and elevated temperatures.
SPS-processed ZrB2 should form a more durable and stable protective oxide layer than conventionally sintered and traditionally lower-temperature-processed ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 should resist prolonged corrosion in a molten Sn-based plating bath better than conventionally sintered and traditionally lower-temperature-processed ZrB2.
ZrB2 retains thermodynamic stability up to approximately 2000 °C.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a fully densified microstructure, whereas the intervention more cautiously targets near-full densification. These are not identical endpoint claims.
